Detailed guidance & important information
Provided as is. Course Atlas is an independent planning aid, with no guarantee that its information or suggested plans are accurate, complete or up to date. It is your responsibility as a student to double-check prerequisites, entry requirements, course availability and programme requirements against the current official programme outline and each course’s official syllabus before making study decisions. Links to official course information and syllabuses are available in the course details.

How to build your plan

  1. Step 1 Choose the courses you want to study

    Use + in the course catalogue to add your targets. The map adds their prerequisites. Select a course to see its details and mark it as already studied if you have taken it.

  2. Step 2 Check and adjust your study plan

    Review your suggested timeline and workload. Drag courses to highlighted semesters, or use the semester dropdowns below the timeline. The planner checks offerings, prerequisites and workload when you move a course.

  3. Step 3 Review requirements and keep your plan

    Check the programme outline assessment and entry requirements. Resolve any unplaced courses and verify details against the official sources. Your choices are saved in this browser; use Download plan to keep a copy and Upload plan to restore it later.

P1–P2: autumn. P3–P4: spring of the following calendar year. A course spanning periods appears in each with its workload split. Provisional offerings reuse outline or previous offering patterns and respect odd/even-year rules. Courses known only from a semester note appear under “Schedule not yet published”, with estimated workload. Official faculty periods ↗

Target placements & status

Drag a course to a highlighted semester to move it. Teaching periods follow course offerings; prerequisites and workload are checked before moving. You can also use “Choose semesters for your courses” below.

Choose semesters for your courses

Choose a semester here or in course details. Choices are checked against offerings, prerequisites and workload. The degree project defaults to semester 4; Mathematics in semester 3 is exceptional.

Review background and entry requirements

These studies sit outside the programme catalogue. Mark a requirement as met only if your previous studies satisfy the wording in the linked official course requirements. Your checks are planning notes, not an admission decision.

The planner uses a conservative, earliest-fit order. Prior participation is placed before a dependent course unless parallel study is explicitly allowed. It checks period credit loads, but not timetable clashes, admission decisions, degree rules or optimality. An unplaced course does not prove that no feasible plan exists.
